instructions: Rinse the rice in a strainer under cold water until it runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and bring to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on.
Slice the chicken thinly across the grain into bite-size pieces. Transfer it to a bowl and add the wine, the salt and 1 tsp of the cornstarch. Mix and leave it for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the broccoli into small florets and the bell peppers into 1 inch pieces. Mince the garlic. Cut the scallions into 1 inch pieces, keeping the whites and greens apart.
In a small bowl, stir together the broth, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and the remaining 2 tsp cornstarch.

Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp of the oil. Spread half the chicken in a single layer and leave it for 1 minute, until it's browned underneath. Stir for 1 minute and transfer it to a plate. Cook the second half the same way.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan, then the broccoli and 1/4 cup water. Cover and cook for 2 minutes. Uncover and cook for 1 minute, until the water has cooked off.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil, the bell peppers and the scallion whites. Stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce again and pour it in. Bring it to a boil, stirring, until it thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute.

Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Cook for 2 minutes, until it's cooked through. You're cooking it to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when the juices run clear.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sesame oil and the scallion greens.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: No version found had 20 or more ratings, so this leads with the best-rated one I could read. The versions agree on a cornstarch thickened soy sauce with plenty of garlic and red pepper; they differ on honey or sugar and on breast or thigh. This version uses thighs, sugar and a little oyster sauce, and adds broccoli for the vegetables. Total is 30 minutes with the rice cooking alongside.
